When Jarris rests on face $F_i$, the farthest point from the table is the opposite vertex, so $k = h_i$, the height to that face.

The probability of landing on $F_i$ is $A_i/S$, where $S=\sum A_i$ is the total surface area. Each pyramid volume gives $A_i h_i = 3V$, so

$$E[k]=\sum_i \frac{A_i}{S}\,h_i=\frac{4\cdot 3V}{S}=\frac{12V}{S}.$$

The inradius satisfies $r = \dfrac{3V}{S}$, so $E[k]=4r = 4\cdot 3 = 12$.

This value depends only on the inradius, so it is the same for every such tetrahedron. The circumradius of 10 does not change it, and the minimum is 12.

ANSWER: 12
